label: Refuted universalized biological gender determinism via Yorùbá ontology
description: In The Invention of Women, Oyěwùmí critiqued Western feminist theory from Beauvoir onward for assuming biological sex universally produces hierarchical gender.
dialecticalTension: Exposes "bio-logic" as a culturally provincial Western visual episteme.

label: Extended Nigerian feminist critique of colonial gender categories
description: Building on Ogundipe’s Stiwanist critique of Western feminism, Oyěwùmí carried the challenge to the epistemological level of Yorùbá grammar and kinship.
dialecticalTension: Deepens Nigerian feminist critique from social transformation to ontology.

label: Formulated Yorùbá non-gendered seniority and relationality thesis
description: Oyěwùmí showed that precolonial Yorùbá institutions privileged seniority (egbon/aburo) and maternal relationality (iyá) rather than Western binary gender.
dialecticalTension: Decolonizes social ontology beyond biological sex.

label: Provided empirical-philosophical cornerstone for Lugones’s coloniality of gender
description: María Lugones explicitly anchored her theory of the "coloniality of gender" on Oyěwùmí’s demonstration that gender was imposed through European colonization.
dialecticalTension: Transatlantic South-South bridge between Yorùbá epistemology and Latin American decoloniality.
